description:
Invite one or more teammates into a workspace, or into a workspace group. Use it after well_list_member_candidates, on the people the user chose.

Pass `invites` — 1 to 20 entries, each `{ email, role }` or `{ phone, role }`, role `admin` or `member` — and a `target`: `{ kind: "workspace" }` for this workspace, or `{ kind: "group", group_id }` for a group you belong to. Only a workspace owner or admin may invite; a caller without that role is refused. A demo workspace refuses both targets with DEMO_WORKSPACE.

Returns one `results` entry per invite, named by its `email` or its `phone`: `status` `sent` (a new invitation), `reissued` (an already-pending address got a fresh link), or `refused` — with `refusal_reason` naming why, ALREADY_WORKSPACE_MEMBER when the address already has access, INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS when the caller may not invite, and DEMO_WORKSPACE when the workspace holds sample data. `invitation_email_sent` is false when the invite persisted but the email did not leave, so offer a resend. Each successful result carries `person_id` for the invited address. Never invite an address already active in the workspace.

Pass `notify: false` (workspace target only) to create or reissue the pending membership WITHOUT emailing — for the assign-then-invite flow where an owner is assigned by a typed email now and the invitation is sent later from the invite card. Use the returned `person_id` to assign that person as an owner without a second lookup.

Pass `delivery: "link"` (workspace target only) when the user asks for an invitation link to forward instead of an email. Well creates the pending invitation for each named address and sends NO email. Each successful result then carries `invite_url` (the accept link) and `role`. The link works once and has no expiry. Every link call mints a NEW link: for an address that already holds a pending invitation (`reissued`), the new link replaces any earlier link or invitation email for it, which stops working. The invitation is made out to the named address, so always ask for the teammate's email first and never mint a link for a name alone.

Pass `{ phone, role }` (workspace target only) to invite a teammate by mobile number, with no email address. Give the number as the user typed it or as a shared contact card gives it; Well normalises it, and reads a number with no country code as a French number. The role is required: when the user named none, ask, and never choose it. Well creates the member's seat in the workspace, pending, for that number and that role, and sends NOTHING to the number itself: `notify` and `delivery` do not apply to it, and `invitation_email_sent` is false. The result carries `phone` (the number in international form), `role`, and `invite_url`, the invitation link that the user sends to that number by WhatsApp or SMS. The teammate opens the link, signs in and accepts, and is then in the workspace with that role: accepting is their consent, and nobody joins without it. Whoever opens the link can accept it, so it goes to that number only. The link works once and for seven days. `reissued` means the number already held a pending invitation here: the new `invite_url` replaces the earlier link, which stops working, the seven days start again, and the role stays the one the invitation already had. `refused` with INVITE_PHONE_NUMBER_INVALID means the text is not a valid phone number: ask the user for it again with its country code. ALREADY_WORKSPACE_MEMBER means a member of the workspace already verified that number.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

delivery.description: How the invitation reaches the teammate. Defaults to "email", which emails it. Pass "link" when the user asks for a link to forward: no email is sent, each result returns a new invite_url, and that link replaces any earlier link for the address. Applies to a workspace target only, and never with notify: true.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

invites.description: The people to invite, 1 to 20 per call. Each entry names the teammate by exactly one key: `email` or `phone`.

role.description: The role to grant on acceptance: admin or member.

phone.description: The teammate's mobile number, as the user typed it or as a shared contact card gives it, with its country code when there is one (+33 6 00 00 00 01, 0033600000001). Well normalises it. A number with no country code is read as a French number.

role.description: The role the seat gives: admin or member. Required: ask the user, never choose it.

notify.description: Send the invitation email now. Defaults to true. Pass false to create or reissue the pending membership WITHOUT emailing, when a later explicit step sends it — e.g. assigning an owner by a typed email, then sending the invite from the invite card. Applies to a workspace target only; a group invite always notifies.

target.description: Where the invites land: this workspace, or a workspace group.

oneOf.description: Invite into a workspace group the caller belongs to.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_invite_members

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. Start the reply with one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

results.description: One result per invite, in the order they were sent.

email.description: The invited address. Present on an email invite.

invitation_email_sent.description: False when the invite persisted but the email did not send — offer a resend.

invite_url.description: Present on a successful delivery "link" invite and on a successful phone invite: the accept link of the invitation. Give it to the user exactly as returned so they send it to the teammate. It works once. On a delivery "link" invite it has no expiry and stops only when a new link is made for the address or the invitation is cancelled. On a phone invite it works for seven days, and a new ask for the number replaces it.

person_id.description: The invitee's person id on a successful workspace invite (sent or reissued). Use it to assign the person as an owner right after inviting, with no second lookup. Absent on a refusal and on a group invite.

phone.description: Present on a phone invite: the number the seat is made for, in international form (+33600000001). On a refusal for an invalid number it is the number as it was given.

refusal_reason.description: Present only when status is refused. Named reasons include ALREADY_WORKSPACE_MEMBER (the address already has access), INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS (the caller is not an owner or admin), and DEMO_WORKSPACE (the workspace holds sample data, so invite the team in the user's own workspace).

role.description: Present on a successful delivery "link" invite (the role the link grants) and on a successful phone invite (the role the seat gives; on `reissued` it is the role of the invitation that already stood, which this call did not change).

title: Invite members
